scope: Welcome41: C2 D2 source-layer proposals; no new inputs or production changes

before.title: PayPal welcome passes Chaarlie and provider subscriber emails separately
PayPal welcome uses a hashed analytics id instead of the activation token
PayPal pending polling depends on the stable token instead of the activationSource object
terminal PayPal activation polling reports a typed payment failure without the token
welcome labels the account email as Chaarlie-E-Mail
welcome only shows PayPal-E-Mail when it differs from Chaarlie email
one-time welcome recovery selects the order activator and neutral access copy
one-time pending polls the provider-neutral activation status route
Stripe one-time welcome renders paid-pending instead of activation choices
authenticated Stripe and PayPal one-time returns pass their derived Personal Plan destination to the shared redirect contract
one-time activation errors render a safe support or revoked state instead of repricing
paid Stripe checkout_one_time_invalid verification failures recover to pending support instead of pricing
a paid Stripe verification failure preserves the revoked return state
unpaid or non-payment Stripe verification failures expose safe recovery without repricing
PayPal one-time pending and revoked returns do not require an account
one-time pending accepts pending states, reloads active, and blocks permanent states
retryable support can poll again while revoked and terminal failure stay support-only
one-time pending timeout is support-safe and never offers repurchase
one-time pending renders the approved calm copy and progress labels
checkout return analytics does not emit completion events without server purchase truth

before.title: persisted Stripe trial denial renders before account writes or destination reads for signed-in and anonymous returns

incomplete and unpaid Stripe returns allow finishing the same checkout
inactive PayPal returns offer support instead of retrying a terminal checkout

before.title: verified terminal denial replaces activation choices and links to real recovery destinations
`${provider} post denial uses trusted code rather than server exception text`
email send failure keeps password input and allows a successful resend
used activation claim leads to normal login without offering another activation attempt
PayPal terminal polling outcome stops pending and exposes support
password saved but sign-in failed offers login with the new password
`${code} retains both password fields and supports retry`
all terminal recovery states remove resubmission and private account details
PayPal pending POST continues status checking and handles a non-2xx terminal result
pending refresh preserves the same return reference
PayPal poll timeout replaces the spinner with status-retry feedback
